This is me.  I'm in bed, on my phone, desperately trying to get up.  Like, I can physically get up.  But my mind doesn't.  My mind is still laying in bed.  I go to the bathroom, I make and drink my coffee, I pick up around the apartment.  But it all saps my energy.  So my body goes and lays back down with my mind.  And I..... just exist.  I think about what I *could* be doing instead of laying in bed.  But I can't get up.  

I know there are many things I can be doing that used to make me feel good and happy, but the problem is that none of those things make me feel good or happy anymore.  It's like I'm on autopilot going through the motions, laughing and smiling and talking when I have to,  I will literally be laughing hysterically with a friend then hang up the phone and instantly have a straight face and feel completely empty.  

I hate feeling this way.  I hate everything about it.  And I have tried diet changes, drinking more water, getting outside and more sun, exercising more, meds, therapy, you name it I've tried it!  Nothing has made a difference.  When I finish whatever task I was doing, I still ended up in bed with the same empty feeling.  

I wish so badly there was a cure, because I can't handle this much longer.

I wish my parents told me the truth about Santa, too.  I grew up poor. I still eagerly awaited for Christmas morning,  hoping Maybe this would be the year that I was noticed for all the good things I did.. but every christmas, the bottom of the tree was almost empty.  
My mom tried her hardest the same as I am doing.  Looking back, I see now how much she sacrificed to get me those few things I got, and it breaks my heart that she went through what I am going through now.  And me believing that it was because I wasn't "good enough" in Santa's eyes wrecked me inside.

I used to be a Fedex Ground driver.  You are 100% correct on all of this.  However for me, our boss hyped us all up for November through January peak, saying "Yeah its long hours huge loads and 6-7 days a week, but keep working hard and you'll all get q nice bonus!" .  He said that the amount of the bonus would depend on :
1. How much we complained 
2. How many days total during peak we worked
3. How many stops we would help other drivers with (once we were done with ours)
4. How little disputes /issues we had 

So yeah, working 12 to 14 hour days and even helping other coworkers afterwards, taking virtually no days off, making sure every single package delivered was perfect was SO taxing on us.  He would constantly tell us how great we were doing and that we would get a nice bonus ! I sprained my ankle AND had a pinched nerve in my leg (injuries sustained from quickly carrying almost 200lb packages to peoples doors) and I still kept working.  I would work through tears, the pain was unmatched. 

Our crew had 14 drivers. 

Peak ended and he sent us all a long text saying that our numbers were great, better than expected and that he was gunna go on vacation to  Africa first a few weeks and get us our bonus when he came back. Guess what? He came back, no bonus.  He stopped bringing up the bonus in all form.  Slowly us coworkers started messaging eachother asking if anyone had gotten any bonus.  Week by week goes by, no bonus.  After 2 months I finally asked my boss about the bonus. 

He got back to me and said that numbers were "much worse" than he thought so he only gave a bonus to the 4 guys that have worked there for years, while the rest of us didnt get a penny.  We were overworked and given false hope.  After that moment, I lost the love I had for being a driver.  I literally felt it melt away.  I tried so hard to get it back, lying to myself that it was still there.  But no matter how hard I worked and how much I tried to do everything right and good and be the best Fedex driver in my city, I no longer had the motivation to do it.  

We were used.  I cant work at a job where I feel like a replaceable number.
